rationale: Do not use the target effective mass as a control or feature.
Do not use the target Hall mobility as a control or feature.
Conductivity and resistivity are algebraic transforms of each other and leak the target.
Forbidden when Hall mobility is computed from same-measurement sigma/(n*e).
Forbidden for conductivity targets when combined with same-measurement sheet resistance to reconstruct conductivity.
Forbidden when the target is the same overlap quantity or an algebraic transform of it.
Forbidden when onsite variance is computed from target Wannier Hamiltonian elements.
Forbidden when extracted from the same fitted spectral feature as the target.
Forbidden when the target is the same spectral or IPR-derived localization label.
Structure file paths identify or reconstruct graph targets and are not independent controls.
Graph construction metadata cannot be used as graph target predictors.
Forbidden as independent graph claims before OI collinearity ablation.
Forbidden unless weighted-degree and OI-preserving residualization is present.
Forbidden unless matched_random_attack_loss and removed_weight_budget are present.
Forbidden as a target if computed using a test-fold fit; residuals must be train-fold/held-out only.
Baseline prediction is forbidden as a feature in raw-label models; it is allowed only to compute residuals.

Executable OI fixed-density rule: pair_density cannot support an independent graph claim unless comparing held-out residuals within bins or matches satisfying abs(log(pair_density_a/pair_density_b)) <= 0.05 and abs(OI_norm_a-OI_norm_b) within predeclared tolerance.

Executable OI fixed-pair versus fixed-density rule: if N_pair changes with volume or composition use OI_norm=sum(Pairs*OI)/volume and include pair_density as a control; if N_pair is fixed use OI_pair_mean=sum(Pairs*OI)/N_pair and do not claim density effects from raw pair sum.
